summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of Supreme Petrochem's Q2 FY27 results and dividend announcement, with most key financial figures and dates aligning with reported information. However, there are some inaccuracies regarding the tax treatment of dividend income in India.

claims.claim: Supreme Petrochem has announced a first interim dividend of ₹2.50 per share for the financial year 2026-27.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm Supreme Petrochem declared an interim dividend of ₹2.50 per share for FY27.

claims.claim: The company's revenue for Q2 FY27 surged by 77.8% year-on-year, reaching ₹1,956.7 crore.
claims.note: Financial news reports confirm the revenue figure and percentage increase for Q2 FY27.

claims.claim: Profit After Tax (PAT) for the same quarter nearly doubled, amounting to ₹94.9 crore.
claims.note: Sources confirm that PAT for Q2 FY27 nearly doubled to ₹94.9 crore.

claims.claim: October 30 has been fixed as the record date for this interim dividend, impacting who receives the payout.
claims.note: The record date of October 30, 2026, for the interim dividend is consistently reported.

claims.claim: In India, dividends received from domestic companies are taxable in the hands of the shareholder. For individuals, dividend income is added to their total income and taxed at their applicable income tax slab rates.
claims.note: Since FY 2020-21, dividends are taxable in the hands of shareholders at their applicable slab rates.

claims.claim: For instance, if her effective tax rate is 31.2% (including cess), the tax payable on this dividend would be approximately ₹3,750 * 31.2% = ₹1,170.
claims.note: This is a calculation based on the stated tax rate and dividend income, which is mathematically correct. The taxability of dividend income at slab rates is confirmed by income tax regulations.

claims.claim: Dividend income up to ₹5,000 is tax-free; the amounts which are above this limit are taxed as per the income tax slab rates.
claims.note: While some sources mention a TDS exemption for dividend income up to ₹5,000, this does not mean the income itself is tax-free. Dividend income is generally taxable at slab rates from the first rupee. One source mentions that from April 1, 2025, the new budget has set up ₹10,000 dividend earnings as tax-free, but this is not universally stated as a tax-free limit for all dividend income, rather a TDS threshold.

claims.claim: As per Section 194, if the dividend payment exceeds ₹10,000 within a single FY, TDS will be deducted at a 10% rate.
claims.note: Section 194 of the Income Tax Act mandates TDS at 10% if dividend payment exceeds ₹10,000 in a financial year.

article_title: Supreme Petrochem Q2 FY27 Results: Decoding the Dividend and Financial Performance
